correctness.rationale: Edge transpositions generate S₁₀ by connectivity; relabeling all tokens carries any start to identity and preserves moves. Every transposition changes parity and the fifteen different edges give distinct neighbors. I independently exhausted the metric using Python layer BFS with two five-symbol direct rank lookups and Floyd–Warshall for graph distances. It processed 3,628,800 distinct states with the exact 18 claimed shell counts, ending in the four strings 7895623401, 7895634012, 8956723401 and 8956734012. These give the stated rail swap with respective shifts independently 2 or 3 and 4·10!/2=7,257,600 unordered diametral pairs. I separately applied the explicit route and obtained the first string in 17 legal swaps. Each move reduces total displacement by at most two; the full census gives maximum ceiling-half deficit 4 at 1,440 states, and B=15 at each antipode. Both frozen C++ implementations were inspected: their different representations enumerate the same 15 neighbors, assign depths by FIFO and compute the correct transportation normalization. They were not executed. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/audit_replay/prism.py; output at /workspace/audit_replay/prism.txt.
residual_risks: This is a complete finite census for unit-cost sequential swaps, not an argument for other prisms or for parallel swapping.

evidence: Tree/spanner and general complexity conclusions do not classify the prism; transposition-tree extremal results apply to trees with different generating sets; circular sorting computes the diameter for a single cycle modulo rotations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Dropping generators for a spanning tree supplies bounds, not equality. Forgetting rungs or quotienting by rotation changes the available moves or the actual state space.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Adding the two wraparound generators to the ladder can only decrease distances on the same state set, so its diameter gives 21 as an upper bound, not 17 or any equality class. The prism antipode form, histogram and maximal-deficit multiplicity are not mechanical consequences of these bounds.

evidence: The nearest indexed prism-sized comparisons instead use GP(5,2) (inner step 2) and P₂×P₅ (open rails). The target is the distinct GP(5,1) with closed step-1 rails.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Position swaps give a transposition-generator Cayley graph; relabeling positions can preserve it only by carrying the edge generators to the new edge set. The open ladder has fewer generators and the Petersen graph is not isomorphic to the prism (e.g. no 4-cycles versus rung squares).

value.rationale: The pentagonal prism is a canonical small non-tree cubic graph with two interacting rail cycles. Its full sequential-swap distribution and structured four extremizers are reusable benchmarks, not just an unexplained diameter constant. The worst transportation deficit and its multiplicity measure the accuracy of a standard lower bound on exactly this graph; notably, worst-gap placements are not the most distant placements. These exact facts are useful even without a formula for larger prisms.
residual_risks: No general family formula, no claim of efficient exact token swapping on arbitrary graphs.
